verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The last snow melts from the roof tiles one drop at a time.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
somewhere a gutter
learns the whole song by heart —
one note, over and over

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a crow interrupts,
tilts its head at the rhythm,
adds nothing, stays anyway

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I sweep the porch clean
though rain's still falling somewhere —
this too keeps its own time

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the kettle starts humming
before I've struck the match —
some things arrive early

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
my shadow leaves first
long before I stand up —
already halfway to the door

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the porch light flickers on
mistaking dusk for someone home —
I let it think so

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I count the mail twice
before admitting none of it
was ever going to be for me

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the phone stays quiet
so I practice how I'd sound
saying nothing back

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the kettle finishes
before I remember what
I was going to pour it for

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
still, I pour it—
into the one cup
that never asks who for

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
steam finds the window
and writes an answer there
before it fades

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
I trace the letters
with a fingertip, learning
a language I'll forget

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
outside, the frost
keeps its own version—
neither of us checking who's right

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the kettle cools
into a small silence
we both agree to keep

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
morning takes the cup
still warm from someone's hands
before the day asks whose
